node_definition.done_when: A new tests/test_route_before_queue.py shows: with an open codex lane and a full local lane, two ready requests the picker routes to codex launch at once and one routed locally queues; a codex-routed request with an unmet wait sits awaiting-upstream with its route and launches on codex when its upstream lands; a codex-routed request that becomes ready while codex is pace-held launches on local with the fallback and its reason recorded on the request and the run; a request dispatched with --backend codex, or whose route was set by crew queue edit, stays queued with the hold named and never falls back; the negative arm routes nothing to codex and every request queues locally as today. Admission also covers every metered lane a queued request is routed to: a codex-routed request released from awaiting-upstream after dispatch launches on codex with no coordinator call, shown end to end in tests/test_route_before_queue.py, whose negative arm (local-lane admission only) leaves that request queued. The test files importing each changed module add no failures against the base revision, measured serially as a delta with the base and head logs under the run directory; ruff check and ruff format --check pass on the changed paths.
node_definition.goal: Route every request through the picker before it enters the one queue, launch ready metered requests at once, and fall back to local when the metered lane cannot serve at launch
node_definition.negative_control: make admission keep a pace-held codex route queued instead of falling back; the fallback arm must fail
